title: THAT YOU MAY KNOW THE EARTH IS THE LORD'S

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses replied, "When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands in prayer to the Lord. The thunder will stop and there will be no more hail, so you may know that the earth is the Lord's. But I know that you and your officials still do not fear the Lord God."" - Exodus 9:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses will pray, and the storm will stop — for a purpose: so you may know that the earth is the Lord's.

That phrase is worth carrying with you. The earth is the Lord's. Not Pharaoh's, though he ruled a superpower. Not ours, though we hold title deeds and passports. Paul quotes this idea directly: the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it (1 Cor 10:26).

If the earth is His, then our possessions are on loan, our positions are temporary, and our anxieties about control are misplaced. It also means creation matters to Him — this world is not disposable scenery.

Then Moses adds something remarkably honest: but I know that you and your officials still do not fear the Lord God.

He prays for Pharaoh without being fooled by him. That is a mature combination. We can be generous and discerning at the same time — kind to people without being naive about them. Jesus told His disciples to be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves (Mt 10:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live as an owner or as a steward of what God has entrusted to me?
2. Can I be both kind and clear-eyed about people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, the earth is Yours and so is my life. Make me a faithful steward and give me wisdom with people. Amen.
